For the petitioner: Mr. Bimal Gupta, Senior Advocate with Mr. Satish Sharma and Mr. Varun Thakur, Advocate.

For the respondents: Mr. Anup Rattan, Advocate General with Mr. Navlesh Verma, Mr. Rakesh Dhaulta Mr. Pranay Pratap Singh, Additional Advocates General, Mr. Gautam Sood, Mr. Arsh Rattan and Mr. Sidharth Jalta Deputy Advocates General, for the respondents-State.
M.S. Ramachandra Rao, Chief Justice
This public interest litigation has been filed by the petitioner for the benefit allegedly of residents of the area abutting the link road Upper Bhager to Kalar-Sarti.

2) He seeks a direction to respondents no.1 to 3 to take .
immediate action for proceeding against private respondents no.7 and 8 contending that the latter are obstructing and blocking the public link road, which was owned and being constructed by the Department of HP PWD of the State Government; and he also seeks a direction to respondents no.1 Laxman Singh vs State Of H.P. & Others on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99149580/
1 to 5 to remove the blockages/obstructions caused by respondents no.7 and 8 and to restore the road,
or in the alternative, to direct respondent no.4 and 5 to complete the construction of the road on Khasra No.87/4, which had already been donated in favour of HP PWD within a stipulated time 3)

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
According to the petitioner, the State Government, in order to construct roads/link roads,
especially ambulance roads, decided to construct such roads in the State of Himachal Pradesh and pursuant thereto decision was taken to lay 31 link/ambulance roads in the 10th circle HP PWD Bilaspur and one such road was the upper Bhager to Kalari-Sarti road.
4) According to him, administrative approval was granted for spending Rs.34.06 lacs by the Principal Secretary (Finance) to the Government of Himachal Pradesh, which was conveyed by respondent no.4 to respondent no.5 on 21.07.2017, copy of which is Annexure P-1.
.
5) In the said memorandum dt. 21.07.2017, a condition is imposed that such new road will be constructed only if the community donate land free of cost and the work would be started only after the land is transferred to the Government.
6) According to the petitioner, in terms of said condition, 27 persons, including the petitioner, have donated their land by way of gift deeds in favour of HP PWD for construction of the road.
7) It appears that the proposed road is also to pass through Khasra No.102/20/2 which is owned by respondent no.7 alongwith other co-owners.
Respondent no.8 is the son of respondent no.7.

8) Though it is contended by the petitioner that that there was donation of the land by respondent no.7 of the said land as well, no document has been placed on record by the petitioner or by the official respondents in support of the said pleading, and in the reply filed by respondent nos.1, 4 and 5 they state that there was verbal consent of the land owners.
9)

The Station House Officer, Police Station, Ghurmawin (respondent no.6) had in fact filed a reply stating that respondent no.7 had no doubt gifted some land, but the disputed road was not laid in the said land and the road is existing on the private land of respondent no.7.

entities.text: Station House Officer, Police Station, Ghurmawin
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text:
He also stated that except the petitioner no other .
villager had sought any right through or over the disputed land, and only the petitioner is claiming the same, and under the garb of present Writ petition, the petitioner intends to get the road from the private land of the private respondents without any right.

This is also the stand of the Deputy Commissioner, Bilaspur (respondent No.2) and Sub Division Magistrate (Civil) Ghumarwin (respondent no.3).
10) In Sukh Dutt Ratra and another vs. State of Himachal Pradesh & others1, the Supreme Court held that under Article 300A of the constitution, no person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In that case, the State had merely averred to the appellants' alleged verbal consent Laxman Singh vs State Of H.P. & Others on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99149580/
2 or the lack of objection, but has not placed any material on record to substantiate the said plea; it had been unable to produce any evidence indicating that the land of the appellants had been taken over or acquired in the manner known to law; or that they had ever paid any compensation.

entities.text: Laxman Singh vs State Of H.P. & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
(2022) 7 SCC 508 11) Similar plea had been rejected by the Supreme Court in Vidaya Devi vs The State Of Himachal Pradesh2 and it was held .
that in a democratic polity governed by the rule of law, the State could not have deprived a citizen of their property without the sanction of law and the State must comply with the procedure for acquisition, requisition, or any other permissible statutory mode;
and the State being a welfare State governed by the rule of law cannot arrogate to itself a status beyond what is provided by the Constitution.
12) The said judgments apply on all fours to the instant case and it is not known why, without acquiring the land in Khasra No.102/20/2 by following the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and paying compensation to respondents no.7 and 8, the official respondents had proposed to construct a road in the said land taking shelter under the alleged oral verbal consent of respondent no.7.

entities.text: Vidaya Devi vs The State Of Himachal Pradesh2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
13) In this factual matrix, we are of the opinion that respondents no.7 and 8 are fully justified in obstructing the road laid through (2020) 2 SCC 569 their land; and neither the petitioner nor the residents of the area nor the official respondents can compel respondents no.7 and 8 to .
allow their land to be used for the purpose of road without acquiring the same by following the due process of law mentioned above.
14) We hold that filing of the writ petition is an abuse of process of Court by the petitioner and other residents who apparently want to coerce respondents no.7 and 8 to give up their right in the said land free, which they are not entitled to seek.
15) Once we hold that the action of respondents no.7 and 8 is not illegal, no relief can be granted to the petitioner in this writ petition.
Accordingly, this writ petition is dismissed.
16) Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.
No costs.
( M.S. Ramachandra Rao ) Chief Justice ( Ajay Mohan Goel ) Judge July 18, 2023 (vt)
